Package org.checkerframework.javacutil

Class ResolverTest

java.lang.Object
org.checkerframework.javacutil.ResolverTest
public class ResolverTest extends Object
Unit tests for how Resolver finds local variables at a path to a tree of the compilation unit. A path that ends with an artificial tree, which is not in the compilation unit, must not be passed to Resolver; StringToJavaExpression#atPath resolves it in the scope of the tree it was created for.

    • treeInSource

      public void treeInSource()
      At a tree in the compilation unit, the scope is that of the tree. That includes b, which is declared in the innermost block, so the scope is neither that of the method nor that of the block.

    • treeInLambda

      public void treeInLambda()
      At a tree in the body of a lambda, the scope includes the lambda's variables.

    • treeInAnonymousClass

      public void treeInAnonymousClass()
      At a tree in a method of an anonymous class, the scope includes the variables of the method and of the enclosing method.

    • runOfExpressionStatements

      public void runOfExpressionStatements()
      The expression statements of a run of expression statements share the environment of the first, but a declaration ends the run: x is not in scope before its declaration, even after the scope at u++ has been computed, and it is in scope after the declaration.

    • constructorCallEndsRun

      public void constructorCallEndsRun()
      A this(...) call ends a constructor prologue, so it is not part of the run of expression statements after it.

    • statementVariables

      public void statementVariables()
      The variables of a for, an enhanced for, a try-with-resources, and a catch are in scope in their bodies, and the lookup returns the symbols of their declarations. A field of an anonymous class hides a local variable of the same name around the class.

    • treeInSwitchWithoutCase

      public void treeInSwitchWithoutCase()
      At a path that the CFG builder makes for a statement in a switch, without the case, the scope is that of the statement, which includes the variables declared in the case.

    • notInScopeInSameMethod

      public void notInScopeInSameMethod()
      A variable declared in an earlier sibling block or later in the same block is not in scope. The source lookup does not find it, and since a variable of that name is declared in the method, javac decides.

    • earlierCase

      public void earlierCase()
      A variable declared in an earlier case of an old-style switch is in scope in the later cases. The source lookup does not search the earlier cases, so javac finds it.

    • tryWithResources

      public void tryWithResources()
      A try-with-resources variable is in scope in the try block, where the source lookup finds it, and not in the catch block, where javac decides.

    • localClassFieldHidesLocal

      public void localClassFieldHidesLocal()
      In a local class, a field hides a local variable of the same name around the class. The source lookup stops at the class, and javac finds the field, so the result is null rather than the local variable.

    • lambdaVariables

      public void lambdaVariables()
      The explicit and implicit parameters of a lambda and the local variables of its body are found in the source.
